predecessors.name: French Fifth Republic
predecessors.text: French Cameroun, independent on 1 January 1960 as the Republic of Cameroon

predecessors.name: British Gold Coast
predecessors.text: British Southern Cameroons, which became West Cameroon on 1 October 1961

ledger.x: 1 January 1960: French Cameroun becomes independent as the Republic of Cameroon.
1 October 1961: British Southern Cameroons joins the Republic of Cameroon.
1 October 1961: the Federal Republic of Cameroon.
20 May 1972: the federation is abolished and the country becomes the United Republic of Cameroon.
1984: back to the Republic of Cameroon.
14 August 2006: Nigeria hands over the northern part of Bakassi.
14 August 2008: the rest of Bakassi passes to Cameroon.

wars.name: Bakassi dispute with Nigeria
wars.outcome: Cameroon won at law: the ICJ judgment of 10 October 2002 gave it sovereignty; the Greentree Agreement (13 June 2006) led to the handover of the northern part on 14 August 2006 and of the final parts on 14 August 2008.

wars.name: Anglophone Crisis
wars.outcome: Ongoing: 'separatists started a guerilla war for the independence of the Anglophone region as the Federal Republic of Ambazonia' and 'the insurgency spread across the Northwest and Southwest regions'.
